nodes.text: Welcome to the Silver Flagon. Beds, board, and quiet — we keep all three. Wipe your boots, if you would.
What can the house do for you?

What I can repeat, freely: Lantern Row is pricing arcane dust like it's snowing coin. The Deep Market talk says the kobolds are digging *toward* something again. And the Queen walked the mere at noon and fed the shrine fire with her own hand. What I can't repeat — well. You'd have to lodge here longer.

Signy — the terrace cook — keeps my best room and pays half in leftovers, which suits us both. Caravan masters. Guildhall clerks in audit season. The occasional Waykeeper too stiff for the chapter house cots. And now and then someone takes the corner room, pays in advance, and asks no questions. I extend them the same courtesy.

choices.text: You know Dunna at the ford?

nodes.text: Dunna keeps the inn at the bottom of the road; I keep the one at the top. We trade the road's news through the caravans, twice a season, and never once put it in writing. Her mother Osa waters the mules at our own gate — you knew that? The day those two are in one room again, pull up a chair. Quietly.
Stew with real beef in it, bread from Signy's ovens, and a short board — a short board means nothing on it is old. Sit where you like.
Warm hearths. The door's never barred before midnight.
